fix.notes: The fix is a single filter in the controller; auth enforcement on the individual routes is unchanged, so no security boundary is altered. The test I added validates the menu partition (demimod vs admin items exist) but does not simulate a full HTTP request with a demimod session — a future integration test could do that. fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

The `/admin/` landing page listed all admin menu items (including admin-only pages like Aliases, Matches, Prizes, Rotation, etc.) regardless of whether the logged-in user was a full admin or only a demimod. Demimods who clicked those links would be redirected to the unauthorized page, but they could still see and navigate to the URLs.

## What changed

In `admin_home()` (`decksite/controllers/admin.py`), the full menu is now filtered before being passed to the `Admin` view: if the session does not have `admin` truthy, only menu items with `permission_required == 'demimod'` are included. Full admins continue to see the complete list.

A test was added to `admin_test.py` to assert that `admin_menu()` contains both demimod and admin-only items, confirming the partitioning the filter relies on is correct.

## How it was validated

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed
- `uv run --frozen python dev.py unit decksite/controllers/admin_test.py` — 688 passed, 1 skipped, all tests in the full unit suite green

Fixes #12709

triage.fix_sketch: In decksite/controllers/admin.py, filter the menu items returned by admin_menu() based on session flags before passing to Admin view: if session.get('admin') is True show all, if only session.get('demimod') is True show only items where permission_required == 'demimod'. Alternatively, add a {{#demimod_only}} conditional wrapper in decksite/templates/admin.mustache using the existing demimod_only property, combined with passing the current user's role into the view context. The controller approach is cleaner and avoids leaking admin URLs to demimod browsers.
triage.notes: The main site nav uses a CSS-class+JS approach to hide admin items, but the admin list page has no such mechanism. The fix is isolated to admin_home() and admin.mustache with no schema changes needed.
